resources.name: Pi
resources.reason: Canonical monorepo, tagged source, releases, tests, and contribution policy.
resources.riskSummary: Main moves quickly; pin release facts to a tag or commit.

resources.name: Pi documentation
resources.reason: Current entry point for usage, security, packages, sessions, extensions, RPC, and SDK.
resources.riskSummary: Latest pages can change; use pinned source for stable implementation claims.

resources.name: Pi releases
resources.reason: Versioned release notes and downloadable artifacts for a reproducible baseline.
resources.riskSummary: A release does not freeze provider services or model catalogs.

resources.name: Pi extension examples
resources.reason: Reviewable patterns for lifecycle, tools, UI, providers, sandbox routing, and policy hooks.
resources.riskSummary: Examples are optional patterns, not built-in features or production guarantees.

resources.name: Pi package catalog
resources.reason: Broad discovery surface for packages tagged for Pi.
resources.riskSummary: Catalog presence is not source review, security review, compatibility proof, or endorsement.

resources.name: Earendil Pi RFC index
resources.reason: Design proposals and state labels for Pi-related changes.
resources.riskSummary: RFC state and implementation/release state are different; verify tagged code.

resources.name: awesome-pi
resources.reason: Bilingual curated directory of Pi packages and ecosystem resources.
resources.riskSummary: Different scope: package/resource discovery rather than evidence-backed operating practices.

resources.name: awesome-pi-coding-agent
resources.reason: Automated, frequently refreshed package and repository directory.
resources.riskSummary: Automated discovery and generated descriptions are not hands-on curation.

resources.name: Pi Package Index
resources.reason: Daily npm package index with searchable maintenance metadata and a public JSON API.
resources.riskSummary: Unofficial automated metadata and popularity/maintenance signals are discovery aids, not quality or security review.

resources.name: awesome-pi-agent
resources.reason: Earlier Pi ecosystem directory retained for historical context.
resources.riskSummary: Archived and explicitly retired/outdated; do not use as a current compatibility source.

resources.name: pi-ecosystem-wiki
resources.reason: Architecture, comparison, and ecosystem notes.
resources.riskSummary: Treat generated or synthesized claims as leads until verified against primary sources.

resources.name: awesome-pi-agent by Traveler0014
resources.reason: Schema-backed generated directory retained as an alternate catalog-design example.
resources.riskSummary: Scheduled metadata updates were failing and content had not advanced beyond the initial June snapshot.

resources.name: awesome-pi-mono
resources.reason: Early manually categorized list retained for ecosystem and directory-design context.
resources.riskSummary: No substantive update followed the May seed, so continuing maintenance is not demonstrated.

resources.name: Gondolin
resources.reason: Micro-VM isolation research and a Pi tool-routing example.
resources.riskSummary: Example is not an installable Pi package; project mount is read-write, Node requirement is higher, and the threat model has explicit non-goals.

resources.name: pi-subagents
resources.reason: Subagent, parallel, chained, background, and worktree orchestration patterns.
resources.riskSummary: Subprocesses, worktrees, and tool restrictions are not OS isolation; parallel writers, inherited environment, cost, and persistent state need limits.

resources.name: pi-crew
resources.reason: Advanced durable multi-agent workflow and worktree orchestration case study.
resources.riskSummary: Dynamic workflow TypeScript is unsandboxed, confirm flags are not human approval, the Unix broker is enabled by default, and state remains after removal.

resources.name: pi-mcp-adapter
resources.reason: Lazy proxy/direct MCP integration for users who deliberately choose MCP.
resources.riskSummary: MCP commands and servers run with user access; secret resolvers execute local commands; shared multiplexers share state and credentials; pin every server.

resources.name: pi-web-access
resources.reason: Broad search, fetch, PDF, repository, and video-access workflows.
resources.riskSummary: Queries, URLs, pages, video, or browser cookies can reach several external services; fallback routes and remote extraction require per-provider data-flow review.

resources.name: pi-agent-browser-native
resources.reason: Native Pi tool surface for agent-browser and real-browser workflows.
resources.riskSummary: Touches profiles, login state, cookies, clipboard, downloads, and screenshots; project configuration is trust-sensitive and the external CLI must match.

resources.name: Plannotator
resources.license: Apache-2.0; Pi extension MIT OR Apache-2.0
resources.reason: Human review interface for plans, documents, HTML, and code diffs.
resources.riskSummary: Optional sharing uploads encrypted ciphertext and introduces link-fragment, history, metadata, and retention considerations; disable sharing for sensitive work.

resources.name: pi-hermes-memory
resources.reason: Cross-session memory, session search, and procedural memory case study.
resources.riskSummary: Persistent indexes expand privacy and prompt-injection surfaces; scanners are incomplete; native SQLite has ABI concerns; consolidation calls a model and rewrites memory.

resources.name: pi-coding-agent for Emacs
resources.reason: Alternative Emacs UI over Pi RPC and a concrete headless-trust case study.
resources.riskSummary: Default frontend policy passes --approve to RPC Pi; untrusted repositories should use an explicit non-approving policy and review shared auth storage.

resources.name: pi-lens
resources.piVersion: current-scope; some compatibility smoke pinned to 0.80.10
resources.reason: Structured LSP, lint, formatting, AST, and tree-sitter analysis.
resources.riskSummary: Lifecycle/build paths download grammars, optional dependency install needs review, mutations need controls, and compatibility smoke is not complete proof for 0.83.0.

resources.name: braintrust-pi-extension
resources.reason: Tracing case study for sessions, turns, model calls, tools, and compaction.
resources.riskSummary: Tracing is off by default; when enabled it can upload raw input, normalized context, output, tool arguments, and tool results, requiring classification, redaction, and retention review.

resources.name: gentle-pi
resources.reason: Large SDD, TDD, review, subagent, and safety operating-layer case study.
resources.riskSummary: Broad policy surface, native runtime postinstall, latest RDD marked unstable, many companion extensions, and explicit same-user threat-model exclusions.

resources.name: pi-extensions
resources.reason: Mixed personal extension collection that may contain individually useful items.
resources.riskSummary: The repository is not one atomic capability; each extension needs separate evidence and testing, while some docs retain legacy links.

resources.name: pi-skills
resources.reason: Historical collection covering browser, Google services, transcription, and APIs.
resources.riskSummary: Legacy package scope/install instructions, no observed CI/tests, and heterogeneous high-permission skills require per-item migration and review.

resources.name: pi-share-hf
resources.reason: Historical session-sharing workflow with several redaction stages.
resources.riskSummary: No detected license, legacy Pi scope, no observed tests/CI, and intentional public session upload create blocking reuse and privacy concerns.
